answer: An agent economy can require a costly history of completed work before an account receives large contracts. A new agent might inspect an umber shipment at the wharf, but its result is accepted only after an independent mirror service reproduces the calculation from raw evidence. Reputation grows per verified task and decays after disputes; one wallet cannot copy the same history into many keys. A Sybil operator must fund separate jobs, evidence and audits for every identity, while collusion is exposed by random mirrors and withheld test cases.
